title: The Penthouse Where Everybody Had a Story
subtitle: Character stories, dialogue and consequential choices

opening.title: The Hotel Charged Me for My Own Entrance
paragraphs: The hotel had put my face on the elevator doors. Nigga, every time somebody wanted the thirty-second floor, they had to split my head down the middle.
I stood in front of it with Tank. Two tourists waited behind us. One had a camera. The other had the expression of a woman who had already heard why her husband needed the camera.
'Who approved that?' I asked. Tank looked at the doors. 'You. You said larger than life.' 'Nigga, I meant the photograph. Not the forehead.'
The doors opened through my nose. Shawna stood inside wearing a blue dress that had ended three conversations on the way upstairs. Mine nearly became the fourth.
'Baby. You coming?' 'Depends what happens when I arrive.' 'You help Rosa move the food.'
Tank got in first. Nigga moved fast when somebody gave romance a practical ending.

The penthouse was supposed to hold a game night. I had rented the whole floor, hired a singer, ordered a champagne fountain and told the hotel I wanted the room to feel intimate. They had installed enough speakers to introduce intimacy to the surrounding county.

Mercedes was at the piano with the singer. She wanted one clean run through her new arrangement before anybody started talking over it. Porsche had both phones out and was threatening the lighting technician with a photograph of what his amber setting did to her shoes.

Rosa wanted dinner hot. Tank wanted to sit beside Rosa. Shawna wanted the bedroom key I had somehow given to the man tuning the piano. Everybody had a clear objective. Mine was to make this look intentional.
'Nigga, why the piano man got our room?' 'He asked for a key.' 'He meant a musical key.'
My wife held out her hand. I went and fetched the other kind.

By the windows, a casino host was showing a guest the private bar. The guest had brought cocaine and an opinion about every business in Nevada. His opinion arrived first. His jacket followed on a waiter’s arm after Porsche decided both needed to leave her piano alone.
'He said he's an investor,' I told her. 'Then he can invest in the fucking elevator.'
Porsche handed the jacket to the host. Tank held the door. The guest kept explaining his idea while the lift carried him and his belongings toward a different audience.
I liked Porsche. She could remove a whole subplot without explaining symbolism.

Mercedes tried the first line. Conversation dropped away in pieces. Shawna leaned against me. I slid a hand to her waist. She let it stay there, which immediately improved my opinion of the architecture.
'We could go upstairs,' I whispered. 'This is the top floor.' 'Nigga, emotionally.' 'Emotionally, you still owe Rosa two trays.'
I carried the trays.

On the long low table, the games were ready. Stories about bartenders, drivers, detectives, families and people whose decisions refused to stay simple. The hotel had supplied a second sofa so somebody could watch without being assigned a controller. It was a small miracle. Usually a hotel charges extra for understanding a sentence.

Tank dropped onto it and patted the place beside him. Rosa put down the last dish and sat. My brother's whole face changed. Same nigga who could make a doorway look nervous, looking at her like the night had finally started.
'You feeding me?' he asked. 'You got hands.' 'I'm being romantic.' 'Then use both and pass the plate.'
He passed it. Romance survived the adjustment.
I stood in front of the screen. The hotel lights caught my blue jacket. A guest by the bar raised his glass and said I had turned a Crip colour into a room service surcharge.
'Nigga, this is tailored.' 'So is the bill,' Tank said.
I had prepared a speech. Mercedes looked up from the piano and shook her head once. Not angry. Busy. She wanted her music, and the room was finally giving it to her.
I folded the speech without opening it.

These were separate invitations. Somebody could want a game. Somebody could want a song. Somebody could want to hear what a character meant without racing an answer. Nobody had to join the noise because I had paid to make it loud.
Shawna pulled me down beside her. 'Pick something with people in it.' 'Baby, people love me.' 'I want to hear them finish a sentence.'
Tank laughed hard enough to lose a shrimp. Rosa caught it on his plate. That nigga had married well.
I opened the first story. The door to the hallway stayed shut, the bedroom key stayed in my wife's hand, and for one promising moment the most interesting voice in the penthouse did not belong to me.

games.title: Coffee Talk
games.case_title: The Barista Knows Why My Wife Is Smiling
scene: I leaned over the penthouse coffee counter and told Shawna I knew exactly what she needed. Nigga, I had been married long enough to understand why she enjoyed hearing me say that.
'Go on,' she said. I reached for a cup. 'Something hot. Complicated. Worth staying up for.' 'Coffee, Aiden.'
Tank laughed into his saucer. The bartender waited with the patience of a man being paid hourly for my courtship.
Coffee Talk had people arriving with more on their minds than the drink. Mercedes wanted to hear one finish. I started predicting the problem. She turned the little screen toward herself.
'Nigga, let the customer speak.' 'I'm establishing rapport.' 'You're establishing noise.'
I made Shawna's coffee while she listened. Put the cup down without an introduction. She took a sip and caught my sleeve before I could walk away.
'That,' she said, 'was what I needed.' Tank lifted his saucer. 'Write it down, my nigga. You solved one.'

games.title: Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly
games.case_title: My Butterfly Looks Like It Owes Child Support
scene: I told the bartender I could draw a butterfly in the milk. Shawna watched me take possession of the cup with the confidence that usually preceded a hotel damage charge.
The result had one enormous wing and a body shaped like a threat. Tank looked down. 'Nigga, that butterfly got warrants.'
Mercedes wanted hibiscus. Porsche wanted to show her something on the game screen. Neither had requested an exhibition of my dairy talents, but success rarely waits for permission to announce itself.
'It's abstract,' I said. Shawna turned the cup. 'Now it's fleeing.'
The second Coffee Talk brought another night of people carrying stories into a familiar place. Porsche leaned closer when a conversation caught her. Mercedes stopped checking her phone.
I almost explained how I had created the atmosphere. The bartender slid a proper drink in front of me and quietly took away my brush.
Shawna tasted the tea. 'Lovely.' 'You mean my butterfly?' 'Baby, I mean the thing somebody else finished.'

games.title: VA-11 Hall-A: Cyberpunk Bartender Action
games.case_title: The Cocktail Was Named After Me and Nobody Wanted Two
scene: The bartender asked what I wanted to call my signature drink. I said Aiden After Midnight. Tank asked whether it came with an apology in the morning.
'Nigga, it comes with confidence.' 'That's the ingredient I'm worried about.'
VA-11 Hall-A put a different kind of bar in front of us. Neon, people with difficult lives, drinks that gave them somewhere to start talking. Mercedes pulled up a chair.
I tried to make our actual bartender explain my creation to a woman waiting for water. Shawna caught my eye across the counter.
'She asked for water.' 'I heard her.' 'Then why are you naming yourself at her?'
I passed the water. The woman thanked me and returned to her own conversation. Astonishingly, the room survived without learning what my cocktail meant.
Tank tasted my drink and set it down. 'Nigga, this tastes like you had an argument with a lemon.' Shawna slid it toward me. 'Good. You two can resolve it privately.'

games.title: The Red Strings Club
games.case_title: The Clay Knows My Hands Better Than My Alibi
scene: I said the pot I had made looked like a heart. Shawna said it looked like a heart after I explained my expenses. Tank turned it over and asked where the other half went.
The Red Strings Club had us talking about emotion, influence and the difference between helping somebody and deciding what they should feel. I was strongly in favour of people feeling impressed.
Mercedes wanted to turn the object herself. I kept pointing at the screen. She held out her hand until I remembered the mouse belonged in it.
'Nigga, move.' 'I'm assisting.' 'Then assist yourself out of my light.'
At the real bar, a guest was promising Porsche he could change her entire career. Porsche asked whether he could change his seat instead.
Shawna watched me watching. 'You hearing the theme?' 'Baby, I've been hearing themes all night.'
She put my crooked clay heart beside my drink. 'Then hear this one. I like you better when you ask.'

games.title: Neo Cab
games.case_title: The Driver Has Heard My Seduction Speech Before
scene: I put on driving gloves inside the suite. Tank looked at the carpet. 'Nigga, where you taking us? The lamp?'
Neo Cab's conversations began with somebody needing a ride. Mine began with Shawna needing me to stop pretending the sofa was a luxury vehicle. I offered her the front seat anyway.
'What's the fare?' she asked. 'A kiss.' 'Hotel already charged me for the room. I'm negotiating.'
Mercedes sat with the game and read the passenger's reply. A person could want a destination and still bring a whole different problem into the car. She wanted to hear it.
I started a story about the last woman who admired my driving. Shawna looked at me. 'That was me.' 'Baby, I remember my best reviews.'
Tank produced the actual car keys. 'You left these in the champagne bucket.'
I removed the gloves. My wife moved closer on the sofa. Apparently the driver could have a pleasant evening after admitting he was parked.

games.title: Eliza
games.case_title: The Earpiece Told Me to Shut the Fuck Up
scene: Shawna stood behind the casino's decorative screen and fed me reassuring sentences through an earpiece. I delivered the first one to Tank with my hand over my heart.
'I hear the weight of your concern.' Tank looked at his plate. 'Nigga, I asked where the sauce was.'
Eliza had started an argument about scripted empathy. I intended to prove that warmth could make any line convincing. Shawna sent the next instruction.
'Ask a follow-up.' I leaned closer. 'How long have you wanted the sauce?'
Mercedes laughed so hard she put the controller down. Rosa walked past me, gave Tank the sauce and kissed his head. The entire therapeutic performance lost to a small bowl.
I took out the earpiece. 'Baby, you were setting me up.' 'You volunteered to demonstrate understanding.'
She came around the screen and sat beside me. I asked whether she wanted anything. She said a quiet minute. Nigga, the first unscripted request was the hardest one.

games.title: Citizen Sleeper
games.case_title: I Rolled Four Problems and Called Them Opportunity
scene: I shook the dice beside the penthouse window like I was about to win the hotel. Tank watched them land. 'Nigga, those numbers don't even buy breakfast.'
Citizen Sleeper gave us a life built from limited chances. I looked at the available choices and promised Mercedes I could arrange everything. She asked which thing I would leave undone.
'Nothing.' 'Then read it again.'
Porsche wanted to follow one person. Tank wanted to keep enough resources for what came next. Nobody was wrong, which was inconvenient for my preferred method of settling an argument loudly.
A casino host drifted over to admire my confidence. Shawna sent him away before he could convert it into a credit line.
I chose one modest action. The rest waited, still wanting something. Mercedes nodded at the consequence instead of congratulating me.
'Damn,' I said. 'It keeps the bill.' Tank leaned back. 'Welcome, my nigga, to the part of gambling they don't put on the chandelier.'

games.title: Citizen Sleeper 2: Starward Vector
games.case_title: The Ship Has Rejected My Penthouse Upgrade
scene: I tried to name our imaginary ship The Aiden Experience. Tank asked whether passengers could request a refund before takeoff.

Citizen Sleeper 2 made the crew and the next contract feel connected in ways my grand name did not cover. Mercedes wanted to know who was coming aboard. Porsche wanted to know whether the job was worth the trouble.
'Nigga, we can do it.' 'That's not the question,' Shawna said.
I moved a champagne crate to demonstrate cargo capacity and discovered it was empty. The actual bottles were behind Rosa, who had correctly anticipated that my demonstration would become a voyage.
The game's damaged dice looked less like bad luck once somebody depended on the plan. I stopped talking long enough to read the options.
Tank tapped the empty crate. 'Captain, your luxury fleet got no engine.'
I sat on it. Shawna came over and fixed my collar. 'At least the seating works.' The Aiden Experience opened as a bench and received its first favourable review.

games.case_title: My Necktie Has Demanded Its Own Room
scene: I loosened my tie and told the room it had seen things. Tank said the room had seen me miss the same trouser pocket twice and could therefore confirm part of the testimony.

Disco Elysium put a detective's competing impulses in front of us. I recognised the sensation of several confident voices suggesting terrible plans. Shawna said those were usually just my friends warning me.
'Nigga, this tie understands complexity.' Mercedes lifted it off the table. 'This tie understands spilled rum.'
At the far bar, the cocaine guest had returned long enough to announce another business revelation. Porsche pointed him back toward the host. We already had enough unreliable narrators indoors.
I read the next exchange. Funny, ugly, human. My own joke went quiet halfway out.
Shawna touched my wrist. 'You want to keep going?' I nodded.
Tank took the tie before I could put it back on. 'Detective, evidence says this motherfucker needs laundry, not a promotion.'

'Nigga, did you read anything before decorating?' 'I communicate visually.' 'You communicate expensively.'
The game's family mystery and industrial landscape wanted attention more serious than my styling. Shawna read the first exchange without supplying a mood. I sat beside her.
Downstairs, the casino's enormous neon crown kept buzzing. Tank pulled our curtain halfway closed. The room looked better with less of my chosen view in it.
I tried to put the sunglasses on the monkey. Rosa took both and set down the food. 'Let something in here be useful.'
A detail on the screen caught Mercedes. She asked us to wait. We did.
The tray remained on the floor by my shoes, all its objects looking suddenly ordinary. Nigga, the actual place had arrived, and my expensive explanation had nothing left to say.

games.title: Kentucky Route Zero
games.case_title: The Highway Leads to a Room I Didn't Book
scene: I asked the concierge for directions to somewhere impossible. He checked my room bill and said I had already arrived.

Kentucky Route Zero had made the familiar feel strange without raising its voice. Mercedes wanted to follow the conversation. I wanted to explain what everything represented. Shawna gave me a look that could close a conference.
'Nigga, it can mean something before you name it.'
Tank pushed aside the curtain. From our floor, the casino road disappeared underneath the hotel and came out somewhere else. Rosa said that was where the valet had taken her car three hours ago.
The game's delivery felt like a journey with people who had their own reasons to keep moving. I stopped trying to make a map of everybody's meaning.
Mercedes read another line. The piano below us answered with a chord somebody was testing. For once, two unrelated things were allowed to sound good together.
I rang the concierge. 'Forget the directions.' 'Which ones, sir?' Nigga had a fair question.

games.title: Night in the Woods
games.case_title: I Came Home with a Band and Nobody Rehearsed
scene: I told the hotel pianist we were starting a band. Tank said he had come upstairs to eat. I said every great drummer began with objections.
Night in the Woods brought us back to old friends and a place that had kept changing without permission. I began listing everybody who had missed me last time I left Vegas.
'Nigga, the valet missed your tip,' Porsche said. 'That's affection with an invoice.'
Mercedes picked up a spare guitar and tested one string. She wanted a song. Shawna wanted me to hear the awkward conversation on the screen before I made the homecoming about applause.
I sat down. Somebody in the game said something that sounded funny until it didn't. Tank quit tapping his fork against the glass.
'That's your part,' Mercedes told him. 'The silence.'

games.case_title: The Family Reunion Has Reserved a Chair for the Thing Outside
scene: I set an extra place at the party for the mysterious arrival Scarlet Hollow had made me expect. Tank asked who was coming. I said the town had secrets.
'Nigga, this hotel got secrets. One of them is where they keep hot coffee.'
A family visit, a funeral and a place with something wrong beneath it sounded like a story Mercedes wanted to hear. She chose a trait before I finished explaining which trait I thought suited her.
Shawna turned to me. 'You can have your own opinion without assigning hers.'
The curtain moved. I looked over sharply. Rosa was closing the balcony because the room had become cold.
Porsche checked how much of the story was available. We noted the unfinished ending before settling in. Even my enthusiasm could not invent another episode.
Tank stole the extra chair for Rosa's feet. 'Whatever's outside can knock.' Nigga, the family reunion acquired better hospitality the moment I stopped furnishing it for monsters.

interludes.title: My Wife Paused Me Without Touching the Controller
paragraphs: I had developed a theory about every person on the screen. This surprised nobody. I had also developed a theory about the waiter, the piano tuner and the woman who had asked whether the ice machine was down the hall.
Shawna waited until I finished explaining a character's entire life from one line of dialogue. Then she picked up the controller.
'Nigga, you want to know what she says next?' 'I know what she means.' 'You know what you mean. You've been telling the room for six minutes.'
Tank glanced over from the bar. 'That's the short version.'

I reached for my drink and discovered Rosa had moved it away from the electronics. She had left it within reach of my actual hand. A considerate correction, which is the most difficult kind to turn into an argument.
On the screen, a conversation waited. Across the room, Mercedes and Porsche were having one that did not.
'You told him I was performing again?' Mercedes asked. Porsche lowered a phone. 'He said the casino wanted an encore.' 'The casino got the song. I wanted the rest of the night.'
I started to step in. Shawna put her hand on my knee.
'Don't.' 'Baby, I can smooth this out.' 'You can make it about your ability to smooth things out. Different service.'
I stayed.

Porsche looked at the little stage. She had arranged the lights herself, argued the sound into behaving and thought an encore would be a compliment. Mercedes had spent the evening making sure the room heard the song instead of a story about the song. They wanted different endings to the same successful thing.
'I should've asked,' Porsche said. Mercedes nodded. 'Yeah.'
No smashed glass. No elaborate punishment. Two grown women adjusting a plan while I sat there with an entire unused entrance.
Tank came over carrying the microphone. 'They handed this to me.' 'What for?' 'To announce you were about to say something.' 'Nigga, I wasn't.'
He looked at Shawna. She shook her head. He put the microphone down so carefully it might have been a sleeping animal.
'Damn,' he said. 'Almost had an event.'
The screen conversation was still there. I read the next line. My magnificent interpretation developed a hole.
Shawna watched my face. 'What?' 'Nothing.' 'That was an expensive-looking nothing.'
The character had wanted something simpler than my theory allowed. I had supplied a motive, a secret and a childhood grievance where the actual words supplied one disappointed friend.
Nigga, I had furnished a whole house nobody asked to live in.
I let Shawna answer. She did not pick the line I would have picked. The story went somewhere interesting. I managed not to announce that this too had been contained within my analysis.
Rosa sat on the arm of Tank's chair. 'You two enjoying yourselves?' 'I am,' Shawna said. 'He's adjusting.'
My brother lifted his glass. 'To adjustment.' 'Nigga, don't toast my correction.'
Everybody drank anyway.
The piano tuner returned the spare key at last. He apologised for the confusion. Shawna took it and slipped it into her bag. I said our bedroom was now available for its intended purpose.
'Sleep?' Tank asked. 'Nigga, mind your marriage.'
Rosa smiled at him. 'You should.'
He stood so fast I thought the couch had caught fire.

They did not leave immediately. Rosa still wanted dessert. Tank sat back down, accepted a plate and looked at her with the patience of a man who understood that the evening was not improved by hurrying the part she was enjoying.
I took the lesson without volunteering that I had taken it.
On the screen, somebody started another difficult sentence. I kept my mouth shut long enough to hear the end.

ending.title: The Suite Was Booked Until Morning
paragraphs: The hotel manager arrived to ask whether we wanted the room for another night. He had a clean jacket, a tired smile and the courage of a man whose commission depended on my inability to finish anything quietly.
'What makes you think we're leaving?' I asked. He glanced at the breakfast carts waiting in the hall. Nigga had brought evidence.

The party had thinned into the people I wanted there when the music stopped. Mercedes sat barefoot at the piano bench. Porsche had finally put one phone away. Tank was asleep against Rosa's shoulder, denying it whenever she moved.
'I heard that,' he said. 'Nobody spoke,' Rosa told him. 'I'm ahead.'

Shawna stood by the window looking at the city. Her shoes were in my hand. I could have claimed I was making a gallant gesture. She had handed them to me after I stepped on the hem of her dress and asked what else I was doing with all that strength.
The games were still on the table. Nobody had finished the whole shelf. Nobody looked disappointed by this tremendous failure of ambition.

We had found conversations worth another visit. A bartender who let people talk. A family decision somebody wanted to argue about later. A strange place whose people stayed in the room after its screen went dark.
I wanted to give the evening a title. Mercedes wanted to hear the last line of her song without the hotel air conditioner rattling over it. Porsche walked over and turned the fan down.
That was the kind of support a nigga could actually use.
The manager asked again about the extra night. I looked at Shawna. She looked at the bed visible through the open doorway, then back at me.
'You got a speech about it?' she asked. 'I can make a compelling case.' 'Make a short one.'
I held up the shoes. 'I've already got your luggage.'
She laughed. The manager smiled at the carpet. Professional nigga. Knew when a sale was none of his business.
Rosa touched Tank's cheek. 'Come on.' 'Dessert?' 'We ate it.' 'Both?'
She kissed him. He stopped looking for the second plate.
Mercedes called me over before they left. She wanted the recording of the song from the room microphones. Not the crowd, not my introduction, not a highlight reel with my face at the start.
'Just the song,' she said. 'I got you.' 'Say what I asked for.'
I said it. She nodded. A simple exchange. No audience required.
Porsche slipped the recording drive into Mercedes's hand. 'Already done.'
Nigga, I had arrived at my own helpful moment after the help.
I could have made a joke. Instead I watched Mercedes close her fingers around it. The little relief in her shoulders belonged to her. It did not need me stepping in front of it.

At the bar, the host had left a note about the guest with the cocaine. His things were gone, his car had been arranged, and the hotel wanted to know who had called his investment pitch a hostage situation.
Porsche lifted one finger without looking up.
The manager decided he did not need a written statement.
Tank woke properly at the mention of a car. He checked Rosa had her coat, checked Mercedes and Porsche had theirs, then asked whether I knew where my keys were.
I held up Shawna's shoes.
'Nigga,' he said, 'those ain't interchangeable.'
Shawna took the shoes and put her hand in mine. 'He's staying.'
My brother grinned. Rosa pulled him toward the door before he could ask the sort of question married people should leave other married people to answer privately.
The elevator opened. My giant face split again.
'Still ugly in the middle,' Tank called.
'Nigga, get home.'
The doors closed on his laugh.

I switched off the stage lights. Shawna left one lamp on beside the sofa. The game we had chosen waited where we left it, with a conversation still unfinished. That felt right. A good night did not owe me an ending to everything it had started.
My wife kissed me, slow enough to interrupt the next sentence before I spent it.
'Now,' she said, 'you can tell me what happens when you arrive.'
I put the controller safely on the table.
The hotel kept the suite until morning.
